sections.html:
Mundelein is a Lake County village 33 miles from the Loop, and the recording for any sale goes through the county clerk's office in Waukegan. Population is 32,680 (July 2025 estimate), the typical owner-occupied home is worth $309,700, and 71.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Owners generally compare an agent listing, a self-managed sale and a cash purchase of the house in its present state.

Housing reflects the village's growth: ranches and tri-levels were built in the center of town in the 1950s and 1960s, and larger two-story houses followed on the edges from the 1970s. A tri-level near the old center and a newer two-story near the village edge attract different buyers, and their repair needs differ too. Households average 2.72 people, so buyers may look hard at bedroom count and basement space. Bilingual listing materials can reach more buyers.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Lake County
sections.html:
Deeds are filed with the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk, on the sixth floor at 18 N County Street in Waukegan (847-377-2575). Fees are $70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, and the only extra charges at recording are the state and county transfer taxes.

State tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-15 is fifty cents for every $500 of value. The clerk names six municipalities whose deeds need local stamps or a signed exemption certificate: Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. Mundelein is not one of them. Most deeds qualify for eRecording, but a deed with a paper PTAX-203 cannot be submitted that way.

The Village of Mundelein posts a Permit Application for building and property work or new construction, plus a Homeowner Project Guide, and takes fee payments online. Contact customer service at 847-949-3283 or building@mundelein.org about a specific project. The main village line is 847-949-3200.

Gather permit records for any addition, deck, roof, furnace or finished basement before you list. An inspector will compare the house with that history, and a missing permit is simpler to fix before an offer than after one.

The village also provides water delivery and wastewater treatment from a Lake Michigan supply. Ask the village about final water billing so the account closes at your sale date.

Five elementary districts divide the village, so the one for your street varies: Diamond Lake School District 76, Fremont School District 79, Hawthorn Community Consolidated School District 73, Libertyville School District 70 and Mundelein Elementary School District 75. Mundelein High School serves the village.

  • Rail: Metra's North Central Service stops in Mundelein with weekday service between Antioch and Chicago Union Station.
  • Bus: Pace Route 574 links Mundelein with Grayslake, Vernon Hills and other stops.
  • Streets: Lake Street, Illinois Route 60, Illinois Route 83, Maple Avenue, Midlothian Road and Hawley Street carry most traffic.
  • Interstate: Interstate 94 is five miles east.

The village hall sits on a 10-acre site next to the Metra station, so homes within walking distance of that area are easy to market on convenience. A typical commute lasts 27.9 minutes.

sections.h2: Diamond Lake, flooding and new construction
sections.html:
Diamond Lake is a 153-acre glacial lake in south Mundelein, used for fishing, swimming and boating. Homes near it may appeal to buyers who want water access, and a lakefront or creekside lot should prompt you to confirm flood zone status before you list. Disclose any water events at your own address on the seller report.

Inspectors test the roof, furnace and sump pump here, since winters are cold and summers can run hot.

New construction is also worth watching. In 2022 the village annexed more than 700 acres of land owned by the Wirtz family, where the plan was to build 1,200 houses and 600 townhomes. Price against what buyers can find new as well as resale houses.

The statutory disclosure report comes first: 765 ILCS 77/20 has the seller answer every item and deliver the report before a contract is signed.

After that, build the closing file with the parcel number, the latest tax bill, a loan payoff statement if applicable, permit records and the village water account details. Judge offers by the net amount and the number of contingencies, since a contingent deal can unravel late.

A cash buyer may close within a short window and buy without repairs. A listing may bring more money but takes more time. Let your deadline choose.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Mundelein
sections.html:
The order of steps is simple, and most of the work is gathering paper early.

  1. Complete the disclosure report under 765 ILCS 77/20 and deliver it before the contract is signed. Add any water events at your address.
  2. Pull permit records for additions, decks, roofs, furnaces and finished basements. Call the village at 847-949-3283 if a record is missing.
  3. Ask the village about final water billing so the account closes on the sale date.
  4. Prepare the deed and the transfer declaration. Mundelein does not need a local stamp, so the clerk's recording fee and the state and county transfer taxes are the charges to plan for.
  5. File the deed with the Lake County Clerk in Waukegan or through eRecording, unless it carries a paper PTAX-203, which has to go in person.

A seller who wants speed can ask a cash buyer for a short closing and no repair requests. A seller who wants the highest price can list with an agent and plan for showings, inspections and a lender's timeline.

Whichever route you take, keep the parcel number, tax bill and payoff statement together so the closing does not wait on a missing page.

sections.h2: What to bring when you record
sections.html:
Bring or upload the signed deed, the transfer declaration and the parcel number. If you plan to use eRecording, check first that the deed qualifies, since a deed with a paper PTAX-203 cannot be submitted that way. If you go in person, the Recording Division is on the sixth floor at 18 N County Street in Waukegan, and the staff at 847-377-2575 can confirm which fee applies to your document.

Ask your title company or attorney who handles recording. In many sales they file the deed for you, but you still need to supply the permit records, tax bill and water account details that go into the closing file.

faqs.q: Is there a Mundelein village transfer stamp?
faqs.a: No. The Lake County Clerk lists six municipalities needing local stamps or an exemption certificate: Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. The state tax of fifty cents per $500 still applies.

faqs.q: Which office takes a Mundelein deed for recording?
faqs.a: The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division, 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, Waukegan, in person or by eRecording through an approved vendor. Call 847-377-2575.

faqs.q: How much does Lake County charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: $70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, with state and county transfer taxes as the only additions at recording.

faqs.q: Which elementary district covers my Mundelein street?
faqs.a: One of five: Diamond Lake 76, Fremont 79, Hawthorn CCSD 73, Libertyville 70 or Mundelein Elementary 75. Confirm by address. Mundelein High School handles the older grades.

faqs.q: How do I start a building permit in Mundelein?
faqs.a: Use the Permit Application and Homeowner Project Guide posted by the Village, and call customer service at 847-949-3283 or email building@mundelein.org with questions.
